chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya and Ali ibn al-Hakam, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from one of the two (Imams) (peace be upon him), that he was asked about the fasting of the Day of Arafat, so he said:
Do I fast it today, and it is a day of supplication and asking (of needs).

key_terms.يَوْمِ عَرَفَةَ: The Day of Arafat (9th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: Why did the Shia Imams not fast on the Day of Arafat?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, the Imam (peace be upon him) clarifies that he refrains from fasting on the Day of Arafat because it is primarily a day of intense supplication (dua) and petitioning God, prioritizing spiritual engagement over physical abstinence. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while fasting is recommended, the unique status of Arafat as a day of divine acceptance makes continuous prayer and asking for needs more meritorious for the Imams. The emphasis on 'mas'alah' (asking) highlights the day's role as a pivotal moment for seeking divine favor and forgiveness.
